title: Two-fibre-product cones and their comparison maps on a general site
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and a small site $(\mathcal C,J)$ [def-weil-pbc-topos]. Use the pseudofunctor and strong-transformation encoding of fibred groupoids of [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. For $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Z\to Y$, a two-fibre cone with apex $P$ consists of $p:P\to X$, $q:P\to Z$, and an invertible modification $\theta:fp\cong gq$. Its canonical fibre functor sends $x$ to $(p(x),q(x),\theta_x)$ in the comma category of $f_T$ and $g_T$, and an arrow to its pair of projections. It is a two-fibre product when all four pseudofunctors have groupoid fibres and these canonical functors are equivalences for every $T$. In groupoids the comma arrows are automatically invertible, so its objects are precisely triples with an isomorphism and its arrows are commuting pairs. Given another cone and maps $i_X,i_Y,i_Z,k$ between its three factors and apex, together with invertible comparisons $\epsilon_f:f^a i_X\cong i_Y f$ and $\epsilon_g:g^a i_Z\cong i_Y g$, a cone comparison consists of invertible projection comparisons $a:p^a k\cong i_Xp$, $b:q^a k\cong i_Zq$ satisfying $i_Y(\theta)\epsilon_f f^a(a)=\epsilon_g g^a(b)\theta^a_k$ in each fibre. For cones on the same cospan, the comparison consists of the two projection isomorphisms with $\theta f(a)=g(b)\theta^a_k$. All modifications are over the identity of the base. No product object is chosen.
